purpose: Newly shipping frontier local-AI systems and obscure RISC-V edge hardware. Vendor model-capacity and performance claims are retained as vendor evidence; unknown power/pricing fields are not inferred.

hardware.model: Ryzen AI Halo with Ryzen AI Max+ 395
hardware.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 16 Zen 5 cores / 32 threads
hardware.quantization_compatibility: GGUF and other low-bit formats are usable through compatible CPU/GPU runtimes such as llama.cpp/LM Studio; exact ROCm support and kernels depend on runtime/version. Do not treat the XDNA NPU as a transparent accelerator for arbitrary GGUF models.

llm_suitability.practical_guidance: 128GB unified memory is well suited to 70B-class quantized models and selected larger MoE/low-bit workloads. Actual usable accelerator memory, context headroom and throughput depend on runtime and OS allocation.
llm_suitability.vendor_benchmark_context: AMD reports May 2026 comparisons versus DGX Spark on GPT-OSS 120B, Qwen 3.5 122B, Qwen 3.6 and GLM 4.7 Flash workloads; treat as vendor benchmark evidence rather than independent normalization.

hardware.efficiency_notes: The 120W figure is AMD's platform TDP, not a measured whole-system wall draw. Independent wall-power tokens/joule testing is still needed.

pricing.note: Windows 11 Pro configuration with 128GB LPDDR5X-8000 and 2TB SSD. Linux SKU is listed at the same US$3,999.99 price; store inventory varies.

hardware.optional_accelerator: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation GPU
hardware.quantization_compatibility: CUDA/TensorRT and framework-supported FP4/FP8/INT8/low-bit workflows are expected to be first-class. Exact GGUF/llama.cpp performance should be benchmarked on shipping systems.

llm_suitability.practical_guidance: 748GB coherent memory is relevant to very large dense/MoE models, long-context agents, fine-tuning and multi-service deployments.

power.note: No whole-system power figure is stored because the public NVIDIA Windows product page did not expose a defensible value in this research pass.

pricing.note: No defensible public numeric price was found; do not infer pricing from prior DGX products.

hardware.cpu: 4-core SiFive P550 RISC-V RV64GBCH up to 1.8GHz
interfaces: PCIe Gen3 x4 in x8 physical connector
hardware.quantization_compatibility: The ESWIN NPU uses its own compiled-model/runtime workflow. Official public examples are primarily vision-oriented; do not assume arbitrary GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ models can execute on the NPU. CPU/Vulkan paths are separate and RISC-V software availability remains workload-dependent.

llm_suitability.practical_guidance: 32GB RAM is enough to experiment with 7B-14B quantized models and selected larger CPU/Vulkan workloads, but general LLM acceleration on the NPU is not yet demonstrated by sufficiently detailed public benchmarks.

hardware.efficiency_notes: The board accepts 12V DC, which is operationally attractive for DC/off-grid systems, but no defensible whole-board LLM power measurement was found. The 19.95 TOPS NPU figure should not be converted into LLM tokens/joule without model/runtime evidence.

pricing.note: Historical launch-channel pricing was US$269 for the 32GB version, but current official pricing/stock could not be verified and that historical number is not treated as a current price.

historical_pricing.note: Reported launch price for the 32GB board through Milk-V partner Arace; retained only as historical context.
